sections.h2: Your selling choices in Stevens Point
sections.html:
Stevens Point sellers choose between an agent, a do-it-yourself sale and a cash bid that takes the house with its warts. Because Stevens Point has a big rental and student market, the condition of the house and the people living in it often settle which route makes sense.

A standard listing fits a house that photographs well and can wait out an inspection and a mortgage approval. A direct cash sale helps when repairs have piled up, a tenant is in the unit, or an estate needs a firm date. Hold the cash figure up against a listing's net, after repairs, carrying costs and months of waiting come out.

  • Owner-occupied house in good order: a listing usually draws the most bidders.
  • Rental or student house with turnover trouble: a buyer who already runs rentals may pay more than a first-time purchaser.
  • Inherited or vacant house: a cash sale ends the drip of utilities, taxes and upkeep.

Stevens Point leans toward renters. Fewer than six in ten units, 51.1 percent, are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home is worth $195,400. Population is 26,377 for 2025, a rise of 2.8 percent over 2020. The city sits on the Wisconsin River and is the seat of Portage County, with the university and Mid-State Technical College in town, which keeps rental demand steady. Your house is its own case, so treat the median as a rough yardstick only.

sections.h2: What a long winter does to a house
sections.html:
Winters in Stevens Point run long and cold, with heavy snow, and the cold is hard on an older furnace and an aging roof, so a buyer's inspector goes straight to the roof, attic insulation, furnace and foundation. Put the furnace service records and every roof invoice in one folder before the first showing, and note the date of any attic insulation work.

The city expects sidewalk snow to be cleared within 24 hours after a snowfall ends, or within 48 hours on streets without a boulevard. A vacant house still needs someone assigned to shovel while it is on the market, or the city can step in.

sections.h2: City rules to check before listing
sections.html:
The city's housing ordinance brochure covers the points that most often catch sellers. Check it against the permit file on your address.

  • Permits are required for most remodeling, including structural work, siding, reroofing, a new water heater, furnace or air conditioner, sheds, fencing, demolition, and electrical or plumbing beyond fixtures. Asking before you start avoids a double permit fee.
  • Lawns and weeds must stay under 9 inches, boulevard included. Unpaid city mowing is assessed to the property.
  • Occupancy is limited to two unrelated adults or one family unless the property holds a specific occupancy license. A buyer planning a student rental will ask about this.
  • Garbage and recycling carts go to the curb the evening before pickup and are stored at or behind the front plane of the dwelling.

sections.h2: What if I have a city Rental Improvement Program loan?
sections.html:
If you took a loan from the city's Rental Improvement Program, its terms require repayment in full before the property is sold. A property in a 1 percent flood plain must also carry flood insurance at least equal to the first mortgage plus the loan.

Phone Community Development early for a payoff number. Pass the figure along to the title company, and it will appear on the closing statement.

sections.h2: Condition report and transfer fee in Portage County
sections.html:
Under Wisconsin law the buyer of a home with up to four units is entitled to a finished condition report, and you have 10 days from acceptance to deliver it. Miss the window and the buyer gets 2 business days to walk away and recover deposits. Estate representatives, trustees, conservators and court fiduciaries who have never lived in the house get an exception. The statute is Chapter 709.

Every line of the form needs an answer or an amendment. For items in their trade you can attach written findings from an engineer, a surveyor or a pest control operator.

The seller also pays the state a transfer fee, 30 cents on each $100 of value, under section 77.22. It is paid when the deed is recorded, and the transfer return must already be filed online. Section 77.25 exempts a few transfers, among them inheritance and a parent's gift-style transfer to a child. A normal sale to a buyer is not on that list, so expect to pay.

The recording office is the Portage County Register of Deeds, 1516 Church Street. A $30 mortgage recording fee shows up in the city's loan program materials, so call the register for the current charge on a deed before you mail one.

A title company typically drafts the deed and files the return for you. If you handle it yourself, bring the signed deed and the return receipt, and ask the register how to pay the recording and transfer fees together.

sections.h2: Getting ready for showings and offers
sections.html:
A tidy file speeds things up. Here, collect furnace and roof paperwork, the permit history for your address, and the lease terms if a tenant lives there. A student rental buyer will ask about occupancy limits, so know the answer before the question arrives.

Plover, Whiting and Park Ridge border the city, so buyers have other places to compare, and a clean, well-documented house stands out. Walk the lot too. Cut the lawn below 9 inches, keep carts stored properly, and keep the sidewalk clear in winter. Open city notices are easy to fix now and annoying to fix under contract. Once offers come in, line up the written terms: the price, the closing date, who pays for title and recording, and whether a loan is involved.

sections.h2: From signed contract to closing day
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, finish the condition report first, since its 10-day clock starts at acceptance. Next, gather the paperwork a Stevens Point buyer will want, since a student-heavy rental street raises more questions than a quiet block of owner-occupants: leases and deposit details if tenants live there, permit records, and any city loan payoff.

Tenants complicate things. A cash buyer can purchase a rental with tenants in place, but ask a Wisconsin attorney how the leases affect your closing date. Closing day means a signed deed, an online return, and a title company that records the deed and clears any liens it finds. Check each line of the closing statement before your signature goes on it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Stevens Point rental house with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Tenants can stay put through a cash purchase of a rental. Gather the leases, rent records and deposit details so the buyer can see the terms, and ask a Wisconsin attorney how the leases affect your closing date.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer fee when I sell in Stevens Point?
faqs.a: Sellers owe 30 cents per $100 of value. Portage County's register of deeds takes that at recording and adds the ordinary recording fee.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for work I did before selling?
faqs.a: Most roofing, siding, furnace, water heater, fence and electrical work in Stevens Point needs a city permit. Contact the city's Inspection and Community Development staff at City Hall, 1515 Strongs Avenue, and ask what is on file for your address.

faqs.q: What if I owe money on a city Rental Improvement Program loan?
faqs.a: Clear the loan before the house sells. Community Development can quote a payoff, and your title company can carry it onto the closing statement.

faqs.q: Is a condition report required if I inherited the house?
faqs.a: Not for a personal representative, trustee, conservator or court-appointed fiduciary who never lived in the house. If you did live there, you owe the report. A probate attorney in Wisconsin can sort out which applies.
